name: Lebanah
overview: Lebanah was a male descendant of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his involvement in the religious duties associated with the worship of God in Israel. Beyond his service in the temple, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The individual is known by the proper name Lebanah, also appearing as Lebana in a related scriptural reference. No specific meanings or divine origins of the name are noted, indicating it is a straightforward proper name without additional symbolic significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Lebanah as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this tribal affiliation and his role as a temple servant.
scriptureSignificance: Lebanah's significance lies in his role as a temple servant within the Levitical tribe, emphasizing the continuity of worship and service to God during the post-exilic period. His mention in the biblical record underscores the faithful restoration of temple duties by the returned exiles. As a member of the tribe of Levi, his service contributed to the preservation of proper worship practices in Israel.
